races.name: Dickie McGuinness Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR 133 for the powerful Mullins/Hayes combination, holds winning form on Good over hurdles, but a genuine hold-up operator who needs the race to be run at a proper clip to deliver his finishing kick — the anticipated steady pace set by Tex Amare makes that hard to engineer; 65 days off is manageable for this yard.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, the latest a comfortable success at Punchestown, leave this gelding well fancied to complete the hat-trick; that form has since been boosted and the stable's strength suggests more to come off just a short break, though this deeper field is the obvious test.

runners_data.name: Evangelic
runners_data.note: Struggled badly in recent starts with form figures of 7-0-0, and while a natural closer by style, this field's composition means he is unlikely to find the rear-rung berth that suits him; apprentice rider Calum Hogan (5lb) and limited trainer strike rate in the 14-day window make this a difficult backing proposition.
runners_data.comment: Yet to threaten in its last three starts for a new yard, with the latest effort at Punchestown hinting the trip stretched its stamina; sporting a first-time hood and best around 7f, conditions here look a stretch given the modest recent form.

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained prominent racer with a second on Good over 16f in his latest run — that recent placing on similar ground and the T14 strike rate of 3/29 mark him as a live contender; Josh Williamson (5lb) is a plus on weight, and his consistent proximity at the business end of races makes him naturally suited to tracking Tex Amare.
runners_data.comment: Successful in bumpers in France, this gelding was worn down late after a mistake-strewn round, finishing second beaten 10 lengths at Cork last time, though that form has since been boosted. A first-time tongue-tie and a powerful stable add appeal despite a modest hurdles tally.

runners_data.name: Pebble Island
runners_data.note: 203 days off the track (with a tongue-tie flag) and returning from a long absence with form figures of 6-U, suggesting jumping reliability is an open question; genuinely a hold-up horse in terms of running style, but the crowded rear in this race means Dylan Kidd (7lb) will need to find a different position, which goes against his natural game.
runners_data.comment: An inconsistent sort across both codes, this gelding unseated last time out and has a little to prove on recent evidence, though conditions and trip both look suitable; a yard short on winners and a mixed profile make it hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Carries a 190-day absence (tongue-tie) and his hurdles form of 8- over 16f on Good offers limited confidence, though he did win over 12f on Good in bumper company; a confirmed closer by inclination, he cannot realistically access his best position in this race shape, and his recent form at McConnell's stable has been poor.
runners_data.comment: Successful in a Listed race on the Flat, this gelding should enjoy a return to hurdles and a shorter trip after finding a stiff 12-furlong test at The Curragh beyond him last time. A first-time tongue-tie may help, with adapting back to timber the only thing to prove.

runners_data.name: Yup Bro
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, with a form string of 0 and a sequence of double-figure finishes — the ⚠ tag here is damning and his going profile on turf with soft/standard experience is largely irrelevant when the finishing form is this weak; McConnell's second runner here, Alex Harvey aboard.
runners_data.comment: Switching disciplines could be the making of this gelding, since modest Flat form may not reflect his potential over hurdles, and he is among the more highly rated here for that reason. A below-par run down the field last time and a yard short on winners, though, temper the enthusiasm somewhat.

runners_data.name: Tex Amare
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore the key pace-shaper — her sole run produced a third on Soft over 16f, so the step to Good is untested but not alarming; Anthony Mullins has a modest 14-day record and Dylan O'Connor (7lb) is a conditional, but the tactical advantage of leading unopposed is the dominant factor here.
runners_data.comment: A promising debut third, beaten 13 lengths in a maiden hurdle at Roscommon, hints this filly has more to offer, backed up by useful placed form on the level in Germany; a first-time hood may help, but the modest rating leaves her hard to fancy from this rank.

runners_data.name: Karlynn
runners_data.note: Has winning form over 20f and placed form over 18f on Good, which maps well to this 2m1f trip on similar ground — E Walsh rides and the horse has placed in three of his last five; his prominent running style makes him the most natural rival to Tex Amare and the most obvious beneficiary if the leader tires in the straight.
runners_data.comment: A comfortable Wexford success last time, achieved on a step up in trip, points to physical progress, and today's trip and ground both look within range; a moderate run of form before that leaves this gelding with questions to answer at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Tex Amare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice hurdle and, facing no genuine pace pressure from any other proven lead horse, will stride into an uncontested lead and set a measured, controlled tempo on Good ground over 2m1f at Bellewstown. Karlynn and Mino Des Mottes will attempt to settle in prominent positions just off the leader, creating a compact early order with the bulk of the field — Beauvallon, Evangelic, Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Yup Bro — clustered in the middle and rear. With Tex Amare dictating a sustainable gallop unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours either the leader herself if she has enough class to sustain the advantage, or a prominent racer with the tactical wherewithal to track and pounce — Karlynn and Mino Des Mottes are best placed to exploit that shape. The field contains more hold-up types than can all race from their natural position: Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Evangelic are genuine closers but have been mapped to midfield because this race shape crowds the rear, meaning they are unlikely to get the late sprint scenario their true style requires and their chances in a pace-dependent shape should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tex Amare Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Tex Amare settles into an uncontested lead and the prominent horses fail to mount a sustained challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: Tex Amare dictates every yard on a kind Good surface, jumping fluently and conserving energy through a steady tempo, then finding enough in the tank over the final two hurdles to hold on; the lack of any rival willing to pressure her in the early stages means she is never asked a serious question until it is too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Karlynn or Mino Des Mottes tracks Tex Amare in a perfect stalking position and delivers a clean challenge at the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: The steady pace set by Tex Amare suits a horse travelling well just off the leader's shoulder, and either Karlynn — who has course-and-distance winning form on Good — or Mino Des Mottes can pounce when the leader is asked for an effort; Karlynn's recent winning form over a similar trip on Good gives this scenario genuine credibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly in the back straight, forcing the field to stretch and creating a genuine gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Beauvallon is the most credible closer here given his OR of 133 and Mullins/Hayes combination — if the race develops into a thorough stamina test, he could pick off tired rivals late; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected tempo from Tex Amare to generate the gap, which is against the dominant read.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If Tex Amare's jumping breaks down or she capitulates suddenly, leaving a vacuum at the front that scrambles the established race order.
scenarios.body: A novice hurdle over jumps always carries the risk of a fall or blunder from the leader upending the expected shape, and with Puppet Master and Pebble Island both carrying long absences and untested jumping profiles, errors could shuffle the entire order; in this scenario any horse travelling smoothly at the decisive moment — most likely Karlynn or Mino Des Mottes — would profit.

watchPoints.text: Tex Amare — watch her jumping closely from the outset; as an inexperienced novice leading throughout, any mistake at a hurdle could unravel the entire expected race shape and hand the advantage to whoever is travelling best behind her.

Karlynn and Mino Des Mottes — both will be jostling for the same prominent position just off the leader's shoulder, and if they bump or interfere rounding the first bend it could compromise one or both of their races before they begin.

Puppet Master and Pebble Island — both returning from layoffs of over 180 days over hurdles; fitness and jumping sharpness are genuine unknowns, and a blunder from either in the pack could create traffic problems for the hold-up horses behind them.

Beauvallon — Brian Hayes will need an injection of pace somewhere in the race to bring his horse's finishing kick into play; if Tex Amare continues to dictate a slow-to-moderate tempo throughout, watch for Hayes to make an uncharacteristically early move to compensate.

races.name: Grimme Ireland Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Laxxio
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Anthony Mullins; 77 days off the track and a fall-interrupted recent form string (F43P3) raise freshness questions, but two placed efforts on Good ground in similar company keep him in scope from a handy position.
runners_data.comment: Fitness is the obvious question given a fall and a below-par run among recent starts, but this gelding showed promise when third, beaten 5 1/2 lengths, at Bellewstown last time, fresh from just a short break; conditions and trip both look suitable if he stays sound.

runners_data.name: Loyal Touch
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Denis Hogan whose last five runs show a pattern of finishing in the bottom half of large fields; 51 days since a last-of-nine finish and no win in 15 Good-ground starts make it very hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Poor recent form has followed this gelding to a new yard, and a below-par effort at Limerick last time did little to inspire; a fair mark on UK form offers hope, with today's trip and ground in his favour, but he has yet to settle since the move.

runners_data.name: Press The Button
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's prominent racer carries blinkers and has a winning run on Good ground at this exact trip; a 39-day break looks fine, and a mark of OR 120 is very workable given his 2/16f/GOO form line — the standout pace-map fit.
runners_data.comment: A promising hurdling debut at Ballinrobe, filling the runner-up spot beaten 6 1/2 lengths after a break, points to more improvement now fully tuned up. Conditions and trip both suit, and cheekpieces go on for the first time, with only limited experience over hurdles the slight concern.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Andrew Slattery who has placed three times on Good in 15 runs without winning; a 29-day turnaround and a lowest OR in the field at 105 give him an opening, but finishing positions of 5-6-3-4-9 suggest consistent but limited.
runners_data.comment: A frustrating sort at times, this gelding failed to complete when running out last time at Clonmel, but he has otherwise been a fairly reliable frame-filler over hurdles; conditions and trip both look suitable, with jumping cleanly the main thing needed to see more.

runners_data.name: Pepper Noir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a massive 537-day absence; the tongue-tie returns and the step back to turf is interesting for McConnell, but the layoff combined with a modest form record (0 wins, 1 place from 15 Good runs) makes on-trust support risky.
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts on the level recently, with a below-par run at Navan last time doing nothing to change that, this mare has plenty to prove back over hurdles; a first-time tongue-tie and only a short break offer some hope, though the recent form gives little to go on.

runners_data.name: Allroadsleadtorome
runners_data.note: McConnell's runner has genuine hold-up tendencies but the crowded rear means he is mapped into midfield — racing further forward than natural for him; a 3/4 record on Good-ground appearances and four consecutive top-10 finishes without threatening the frame cap the ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Modest efforts have followed this gelding's hurdling debut, with the Downpatrick run last time showing little progress; a yard without a winner recently adds to the concerns, though he does act well on heavy and today's conditions and trip suit. More time looks needed before he's competitive.

runners_data.name: Highland Realm
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends a lightly raced 5yo with just one career run — a promising second on Good — for his stable; 323 days absent is the obvious concern, but Mullins' record with held-back ammunition means this runner cannot be ignored despite the unknown fitness level.
runners_data.comment: A narrow runner-up on his only start, beaten half a length in a bumper at Tramore, this gelding was sent off favourite but had to settle for second. A lengthy absence since is the concern, but a powerful stable suggests more to come now switching to hurdles, with conditions and trip both suiting.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: T Hogan's prominent racer has placed in six of ten Good-ground starts and shows a remarkably consistent 3-2-2-3-3 recent run of results; the 5-runner amateur jockey claiming 5lbs rides, and the consistent placed profile over this exact trip makes him a model fit for the dominant pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistency is the calling card, with frame finishes including third, beaten 3 1/4 lengths, at Sligo last time continuing a pattern set since a solid debut defeat by a useful rival. Conditions look no obstacle, and a first-time hood may help find the finishing effort still missing.

runners_data.name: Million Dollar Man
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner for Thomas Corish; his form reads P-60 and he has finished 21st and 6th from two runs on Good ground, so he is a weak pace-setter in terms of ability — but his role as sole dictator is secure, and that tactical position alone makes him relevant to the race shape.
runners_data.comment: A drop in trip did this gelding no favours at Punchestown last time, where the pace proved too hot down the field; he looks better suited by further and more of a fit for handicaps. A return to a stiffer trip is likely needed to show his real form.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Millar who has run in large fields on Good ground nine times from eleven starts without a win or place in this company; 20 days between runs keeps him fit but the form trajectory (4-6-4-6-7) is one of moderate consistency without acceleration.
runners_data.comment: A modest hurdling debut at Downpatrick, hampered by jumping errors, leaves this gelding needing to bounce back, with inconsistent bumper form before that offering little encouragement either; conditions and trip both look fine, but there is little in the book yet to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a second from 12 Good-ground runs; naturally a hold-up horse but the congested rear maps him into midfield for this race — a role that doesn't play to his strengths even if the style-fit score of 0.92 suggests only a minor displacement.
runners_data.comment: On his best form this gelding carries a fair mark, but there's no hiding from a well-held effort in a handicap at Kilbeggan last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and he's fresh from just a short break, though he needs to rediscover that form to feature.

runners_data.name: Matcho d'Agrostis
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 4yo has fallen twice in three runs on Good and shows a fade-in-finish flag; the amateur jockey at 7lbs claim is a positive weight consideration, but two career falls over hurdles and a 0/3 Good-ground record present obvious concerns.
runners_data.comment: Two fallen finishes preceded a well-beaten run at Punchestown last time, painting a difficult recent picture, even though his debut form has since been boosted at a higher level. He still has plenty to prove and looks more of a fit for a lowly handicap than a factor here.

runners_data.name: The Flying Rambler
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo for J P Dempsey with one career run — a 7th on Good — and the lightly raced flag is the entire story here; unknown running style and unraced over this trip make assessment speculative.
runners_data.comment: Racing too keenly proved the undoing of this gelding on his only start, a well-beaten bumper run here, and there's plenty to find educationally now switching to hurdles. A first-time hood may aid settling, and he's fresh from just a short break, but the concerns are obvious.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on this prominent 4yo; a 0/8 record on Good ground and a 20th-of-20 last outing on Soft is concerning, but a second on Soft and a third on Soft show he handles cut — Good may not be ideal, though the Kennedy/Elliott combination demands respect.
runners_data.comment: A below-par effort last time out follows a game third, beaten just a length, in a conditions event at The Curragh that shows this gelding can mix it at a good level, and cut in the ground should suit. First-time cheekpieces and a powerful stable add interest, though he can be tricky to fathom.

runners_data.name: Double Order
runners_data.note: Has a genuine hold-up profile but carries a fading-in-finish flag and is mapped into midfield given the overcrowded rear; three runs on Good have produced a 6th, 9th and 11th, and the tendency to fade rather than finish makes this scenario-dependent at best.
runners_data.comment: A below-par effort up in trip down the field in a bumper at Wexford last time leaves plenty to find on this mare's hurdling debut, and conditions alone won't be enough to turn things round; she remains an unknown quantity at best on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Getaway Tobin
runners_data.note: McConnell's hold-up type has run three times on Good without threatening a place (5-4-12); 21 days between runs suggests freshness is not an issue, but the form figures give little reason to elevate him above speculative interest.
runners_data.comment: Modest bumper form, capped by a well-held run at Hexham last time, gives little to work with for this mare's switch to hurdles, though earlier flickers of promise suggest more may follow. A first-time tongue-tie and suitable conditions offer some hope, but a yard short on winners doesn't help.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a fading-in-finish tag and a single run in this campaign finishing 12th on Good; the flat-racing background (7 of 15 runs on Standard ground) and winless career record over hurdles make this a very difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort on his hurdling debut at Ballinrobe last time gives little encouragement, and this gelding otherwise looks up against stronger rivals on this form; his best form to date has come around 13 furlongs, so today's test remains an open question rather than a formality.

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: McConnell fields a fourth runner here; a hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish flag, one run on Good (12th of 17) and an OR of 120 that looks aspirational given the evidence — the trainer volume is noted but this runner is the weakest of the stable's quartet on current form.
runners_data.comment: A modest introduction down the field in an amateur riders' bumper at Aintree last time leaves this gelding needing to step forward on both his point-to-point and bumper form. He's fresh from just a short break, but there's little in the book yet to inspire real confidence.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Patrick Rooney with no last-run data, unknown going preference and a lightly raced flag; the amateur 7lb claimer Alix Balfe takes the ride and the lowest weight in the field at 147lbs provides a theoretical edge — but first-time-out hurdlers in 19-runner maiden fields face a stiff ask.
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Poet's Word making her debut, this filly is a half-sister to Shirley's The Boss, who found 16 furlongs too far, and the stable isn't renowned for a strong hit-rate under rules. With no bumper experience behind her, she looks one to watch rather than back with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Million Dollar Man is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise him, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m1f at Bellewstown — a track that rewards jumping ability and stamina rather than raw speed. The field is large at 19 runners but the pace map is thin up front, meaning Million Dollar Man can control tempo and dictate a measured race that could compress the field and keep the pace genuine-but-not-scorching through the closing stages. Prominent racers who can travel close to the fractions without expending energy — Press The Button, Highland Realm, Hopeful Hero, Wackestone and Laxxio — are best positioned to exploit that shape, arriving at the final two hurdles with something in reserve. Double Order, Allroadsleadtorome and Kasper Hauser are true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield on the map because the back markers are already filled; they are unlikely to secure their natural deep position, and the closers' scenario is consequently weakened — this race shape most clearly favours prominent, galloping types who can sit just off a lone, uncontested front-runner and pick him up from two out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Million Dollar Man bowls along uncontested and sets a genuine-but-measured pace that stretches the field without burning off the prominent chasers.
scenarios.body: Million Dollar Man dictates every fraction and the prominent horses immediately behind him — Press The Button, Hopeful Hero and Highland Realm — travel into contention without fuss, jumping from 2-3 out to challenge; the winner comes from the lead or just off it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Track Gallopers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to crack any stayer short of gas, allowing the best-travelling prominent horse to cruise past Million Dollar Man from 3 out.
scenarios.body: The lead turns over smoothly to a prominent racer with proven stamina on Good ground; Press The Button's winning course-and-distance form on Good and Hopeful Hero's string of placed efforts at this trip make them the most dangerous beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Survivor Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If a stronger-than-expected pace causes attrition through the race, allowing a well-held midfield runner to emerge through beaten horses in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A true midfield type who has been tracking patiently — Kasper Hauser or Paymelater — threads through gaps as the front rank ties up jumping the last two hurdles; this shape requires enough genuine pace to hurt the leaders, which the thin front-running contingent makes slightly unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly collapses and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish from the home turn that theoretically suits a hold-up horse arriving late.
scenarios.body: Double Order, Allroadsleadtorome and Sunny Dude carry the fading-in-finish flag and none have shown the form to suggest a dramatic late surge; this scenario is structurally weak because the redistributed closers are racing out of their ideal position and lack the raw form figures to capitalise even if pace plays into their hands.

watchPoints.text: Million Dollar Man controls tempo unchallenged — watch whether he quickens at the top of the straight or is swallowed up two out, as every scenario pivots on how long his lead lasts.

Press The Button and Hopeful Hero are the two horses whose prominent style most naturally matches the pace shape — if either travels conspicuously well rounding the home turn, they are the primary threats to the lead.

Highland Realm is 323 days absent and lightly raced, but Willie Mullins rarely runs horses cold without readying them — watch the market and the horse's demeanour in the paddock for any indication of a primed comeback.

Matcho d'Agrostis has fallen twice in three hurdle starts; with 19 runners on Good ground at a sharp track, a loose horse or early faller could disrupt the pack significantly — a risk to frame-fancied prominent types.

Willows Word is a first-time-out debutant in a wide-open 19-runner field; watch if the Rooney yard has supported it in the market, as any unexpected support on an unknown would carry information value.

races.name: Street Sweep Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Becasse
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's lightly-raced five-year-old returns 33 days after a fall, honest Good-ground form (2/16f/GOO in latest comparable start), and is redistributed to hold-up here despite being a true midfield type — watch for a clean jumping round being the priority.|
runners_data.comment: A narrow defeat off a lower mark at Listowel last time, beaten just half a length, keeps this gelding firmly involved on solid recent form including a win among his last four. The yard is in good form and a first-time tongue-tie adds appeal on a fair mark, though he must prove he can turn placed efforts into victories at this level.

runners_data.name: Fiver Friday
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's six-year-old boasts an outstanding Good-ground record (13/15 sim-going, 2 wins 6 places) and 77 days off since a hurdles run, but the 14-day trainer strike rate of 1/32 is a mild concern; a natural prominent racer with the quality to hold that position in this field.|
runners_data.comment: A useful mare in both codes, she was successful by 4 1/4 lengths off a much lower mark last time out. Now racing off a career-high rating, a well-beaten run on the level three starts back under a stiffer mark is a mild concern, though conditions and trip suit.

runners_data.name: Ifiwerearichman
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's eight-year-old has won twice over this distance on Good, returned 38 days after a 3rd and carries prominent headgear — a consistent traveller at the trip who should hold a place in the first six without difficulty.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed recent record, including a pulled-up run and a fall, is balanced by a solid third, beaten 4 1/4 lengths, in a rated event at Wexford last time, fresh from a break. Conditions and trip both suit, first-time cheekpieces may sharpen him, and there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and has 116 days off, two previous wins on Good, but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects that it is racing out of its natural role as a leader rather than a prominent runner; class advantage is real, stamina at 2m1f hurdles needs proving.|
runners_data.comment: A progressive sort on the Flat, this gelding found a stiff mark too strong in a juvenile handicap hurdle at Cheltenham last time, but he drops back in company today for a powerful stable. A first-time tongue-tie and time off add slight uncertainty, though he rates among the leading players.

runners_data.name: Encanto Bruno
runners_data.note: John McConnell's well-travelled eight-year-old ran just 19 days ago, excellent Good-ground record (11/15, 4W 7P), and holds a natural prominent profile — likely to find the prominent berths too competitive but has the form to be dangerous in the right trip.|
runners_data.comment: A modest run of finishes includes a well-held effort at Kilbeggan last time, where racing too freely took its toll on stamina; today's drop back in trip could suit a formerly useful sort, and ground on the sounder side is needed, though a yard short on winners doesn't inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: AJ Martin's six-year-old won over 16f on Good last time, 33 days ago, and the Good-ground figures (8/15, 2W 3P) are solid; runs from a natural prominent position and should get into a decent spot in the first half of the field.|
runners_data.comment: A success by half a length off a much lower mark here in April has since been backed up by a solid third, beaten 4 lengths, off the same mark last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and this gelding looks capable of better again with more positive tactics.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: C Byrnes's seven-year-old won this course/distance/going combination (1/16f/GOO) on his latest start — a strong 33-day return angle and active yard (T14: 3/7); a genuine prominent racer whose recent win sets a high benchmark on this identical surface.|
runners_data.comment: Back to form since getting off the mark over hurdles, this gelding was suited by better ground when winning a handicap at Listowel last time. Conditions and trip both suit again, and first-time cheekpieces add interest, though he rates only the outsider of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old hasn't run since May (67 days, 24F fitness flag) and the 0.92 style-fit flag tells the real story — naturally prominent but forced wider and further back by the overcrowded field; the layoff combined with a compromised draw in the running order is a double discount.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed recent record for this gelding includes a below-par effort at Limerick last time, where going too soon proved costly, though a win is also among his last five starts; conditions look suitable, but climbing too high in the weights back over hurdles is the obvious concern here.

runners_data.name: Lisnamult Lad
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's nine-year-old has a troubled recent form string (FP9P-P) and while the Good-ground record logs a win, the prominent headgear and string of failures late in races makes this one of the harder profiles to trust in a competitive 19-runner field.|
runners_data.comment: A run of setbacks, capped by failing to complete in a handicap hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, leaves this gelding with plenty to prove, and he may be better suited by fences long-term. Front-running tactics play to his strengths and first-time cheekpieces could help, but stamina beyond 2 1/2 miles remains unproven.

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's eight-year-old won 20 days ago (1/16f/GOO) and has an outstanding Good-ground record (12/15, 3W 6P) — a natural prominent type who has done his talking on this very surface and distance; the 20-day quick return merits monitoring but the form is compelling.|
runners_data.comment: A win among his last five starts underpins this gelding, and he did well to hold his position at Downpatrick last time, back from a break, before one proved too good. Conditions look suitable and a first-time tongue-tie is fitted, but he otherwise rates towards the back of this field on official figures.

runners_data.name: Come On The Lads
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's six-year-old carries prominent headgear and won over an extended trip (1/18f/SOF) last time, but naturally wants to race handily and the redistribution to midfield — combined with a 0.93 style-fit tag — reflects how unlikely it is to get that spot with 10+ rivals fighting for the same ground.|
runners_data.comment: A useful sort in both codes, this gelding's fair hurdles mark looks the more promising context after a below-par Flat return down the field at The Curragh last time; conditions look suitable, and a win remains among his last five starts, with first-time cheekpieces added for this switch back.

runners_data.name: Malbay Madness
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's six-year-old has won two on the bounce on Good ground (1/18f/GOO, 1/16f/GOO) and holds hold-up headgear; though the 0.88 style-fit reflects a mismatch with the mapped position, it has the freshest winning form in the field and connections are clearly in form (T14: 0/1 but very small sample).|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins feature among this gelding's last five starts, the latest a comfortable success by 4 lengths off a lower mark at Downpatrick, and there's scope for more physical progress yet. Conditions and trip both suit and a first-time hood is added, though he rates only a modest chance on official figures.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: JP Dempsey's eight-year-old returns after 91 days off and races predominantly on Soft ground (4 of last 5 runs on SOF); the genuine prominent racer finds itself squeezed into midfield by the overcrowded field, and the going question on Good is a meaningful caveat here.|
runners_data.comment: A generally consistent mare with two wins among her last five starts, she found the level too high when well beaten in a valuable handicap at Fairyhouse last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and she's fresh from just a short break, though her mark looks to have crept above her true level.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Yvonne Latta's seven-year-old hasn't run for 63 days, and the form string (1/32F-) includes a fall last time; naturally wants to be prominent, but the race map redistributes it to midfield — a lightly-handled yard (T14: 0/0) with no recent confidence to lean on.|
runners_data.comment: A leading contender on class, this mare was travelling like the one to beat when falling in a Listed handicap hurdle at Punchestown last time, and that placed form marks her out as progressive and well treated. Decent ground suits, she's fresh from just a short break, and the fall remains her only recent blemish.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's seven-year-old is the one confirmed hold-up type in the field (style=H) but comes off a PU last time and 28 days ago, with a blinkers flag suggesting concentration issues; a true closer who would benefit from a strong pace but the jumping consistency is not reliable.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed campaign continues for this gelding, who failed to complete after unseating in a handicap chase at Punchestown last time; blinkers go on for the first time as connections switch back to hurdles, though a stiff mark and unproven stamina for this longer trip leave obvious questions.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old ran just 28 days ago (2nd, 16f/GOO) and the high-class handler angle is clear, but it is a natural prominent racer mapped to midfield because of the overcrowded early positions — the 0.93 style-fit flag means its chance is tempered unless it manages to push closer than mapped.|
runners_data.comment: A consistent sort who found only 4 1/4 lengths too much when runner-up in a novice hurdle at Punchestown last time, this gelding carries a mark that already demands plenty, and a win features among his last five starts; conditions and trip both suit, though the stable is currently short on winners.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor's seven-year-old has the best Going fit of the field (sim-going: 14/15) and was 4th last time at 17f/GOO, but is displaced into midfield by the weight of prominent runners ahead of it; the lowest weighted horse in the top section and a junior rider (7lb claim) make this speculative.|
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort in a handicap hurdle at Listowel last time continues a modest recent run, and there's a sense his mark already reflects his form. Conditions and trip both suit and a first-time tongue-tie is added, but little in recent starts inspires much confidence.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's seven-year-old has no jockey declared, is unmarked UNKNOWN style, and the form (554/0-) includes a long blank and a 14th last time; the Good-ground record (4/6 placed) is the one positive but the unknown style and absent rider are clear planning obstacles.|
runners_data.comment: A needed run showed in this gelding's last start, ridden too prominently down the field in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown, though that experience should sharpen him for today. A fairly consistent sort in maidens who may do better now handicapping, he returns from just a short break with a first-time tongue-tie, but he still rates near the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins's seven-year-old won last time (1/16f/GOO, 39 days ago) and carries a 0.91 style-fit tag as a natural prominent racer squeezed to midfield; the Good-ground winning form is fresh and the 3W6P record on similar ground is strong, but whether it can reproduce that from further back than ideal is the key question.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins feature among this mare's last five starts, the latest an easy success by 8 lengths off a lower mark after dropping in grade at Ballinrobe, and she looks well treated on the strength of previous graded form. Conditions here suit, though a fall earlier this campaign and the step up in company today leave a little still to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Barbizon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground at Bellewstown — the pace will be honest but not frantic, as no rival is likely to seriously challenge for the lead. Behind him, the prominent positions will be aggressively contested: Fiver Friday, Ifiwerearichman, Spy, Red Glory, and Putapoundinthejar are all genuine prominent racers who will be pushing for the early berths, while Autumn Twist, Come On The Lads, Missus Beeton, Thisistheway, Playtime, Fast Felix, Malbay Madness, and Paul's Dream are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position in a field this large and will be shuffled wider and further back than ideal. In a race where the pace is controlled rather than searching, and the prominent slots will be monopolised by a competitive group of genuine front-rankers, horses able to travel in the first five or six on a true Good surface — Fiver Friday, Spy, and Red Glory — are best placed, while those who end up held up against their will carry a meaningful style discount. This race shape most favours consistent prominent racers with proven Good-ground speed who can hold their position from flag to finish without being crowded out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Barbizon Dictates, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Barbizon sets a controlled lead and the prominent battle resolves cleanly, allowing the strongest travellers to sit handy and pounce.
scenarios.body: Barbizon rolls along at a fair clip on Good ground and the genuine prominent types — Fiver Friday, Spy, Red Glory — settle into their natural positions, tracking him with cover and using their pace ratings to kick at the last flight; Good ground form here vindicates the prominent profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Overcrowded Prominent Zone Causes Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the fierce battle for prominent positions creates scrimmaging early, elevating the tempo and catching front-rankers flat-footed in the straight.
scenarios.body: With so many genuine prominent types fighting for the same ground, Barbizon's control is disrupted and the race gets strung out; horses who manage to sit just off the scrimmage with a clear run — including Paul's Dream and Playtime, despite their redistribution discount — can pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Malbay Madness Holds Winning Ticket
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late challenge from a horse sitting just off the action with a strong recent form line.
scenarios.body: Malbay Madness arrives on the back of two wins and, though mapped to hold-up against its more prominent natural style, a proper gallop on Good ground suits its finishing pattern; if riders misjudge the pace, this course-ground profile and recent form could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Barbizon Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Barbizon is allowed a soft, completely uncontested lead with no prominent rival willing to commit pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Given 116 days off and with a style-fit concern, this is a low-probability outcome, but if all rivals sit back and gift the front, Barbizon's class on Good ground with a soft early fractions could see him difficult to reel in up the straight.

watchPoints.text: Spy and Red Glory are both recent Good-ground winners over this exact trip and are likely to fight for the same prominent berths — watch for a bumping/checking incident between stalls 6-8 as they establish their positions early.
Barbizon's 116-day absence means fitness is unverified; if it weakens from the final flight, the entire front-running scenario unravels and a prominent chaser gets a gift lead into the straight.

The cluster of seven redistributed prominent types — Autumn Twist, Come On The Lads, Missus Beeton, Thisistheway, Playtime, Fast Felix, Paul's Dream — will cause early traffic issues; watch the first two flights for fallers or hampered runners from this group.
Missus Beeton has run four of its last five on Soft ground and this Good surface represents a potential question mark — worth tracking in-running to see if it is travelling with its usual fluency.

Stuntman Steve is the only confirmed hold-up horse in a race with almost no true closers; if the pace is strong enough to set up a late run, it is the one horse in the field whose style genuinely suits the scenario — but the PU last time and jumping concerns are live risks.

races.name: Johnny's Race Day Mares Maiden Hurdle
holdup: Uno Me I Like My T

runners_data.name: Bold Reflection
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a win at 16f on Heathery and a fade flag; prominent in style but a big-field 2m4½f maiden at this age raises questions, and the absence of a win in four similar-going runs is telling.
runners_data.comment: A bumper winner, this mare's form has dipped over hurdles, mistakes contributing to a well-beaten effort at Punchestown last time. Two miles on softer ground should suit, and connections were successful in this race a year ago, but she needs to recapture that bumper-winning spark now over hurdles to feature.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Jack Kennedy in the saddle — the key pace-setting rival to Jet To Glory; five runs on Good, two placed efforts, and the tongue-tie is in place; if she controls the early fractions she remains dangerous throughout.
runners_data.comment: Considered a leading threat, she was below her best in an under-par third, beaten ten lengths at Downpatrick last time. Suited by two miles three on yielding and sporting a first-time hood, though repeating that recent dip would be the obvious concern up in this company.

runners_data.name: Chisel Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ian Donoghue's yard, placed in two of three Good-ground runs including a second at 2m, and the step up to 2m4½f looks within range; sits in a sweet spot positionally if the front pair cook each other.
runners_data.comment: Race-fit and rated competitive after finishing second, beaten six and a half lengths, at Limerick last time following a drop in grade. Effective at two miles three on heavy and with today's trip covered before, though three runs without a win leaves a query over sealing it.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Emmet Mullins wearing a tongue-piece, with a third at 2m6f on Good already to her name; the longer trip is a plus and Ricky Doyle can afford to sit and wait if the contested pace unfolds as expected.
runners_data.comment: Having shown ability in points, she made a fair hurdles bow, only tiring up in trip when third at Tramore last time. Cheekpieces and a tongue-tie are added for the first time, and with two and a half miles suiting, there's more to come from this maiden.

runners_data.name: Glendaars Crystal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown style and only two runs (both 2m on Good, finished 11th and 7th); the significant step up in trip is untested and the handler's 0-from-1 14-day record gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Only two starts so far, both below the pace, most recently finishing unplaced after failing to progress from a seventh-placed hurdles debut at Punchestown. Everything remains to be proven on this scant evidence, and with little else to go on she's tricky to trust in this company.

runners_data.name: Idaho Expresso
runners_data.note: Style uncertain, one run on Good in the formbook (unfinished); has a fall and a pulled-up on record which clouds confidence, and D M Christie's two-runner 14-day strike rate offers little angle.
runners_data.comment: A winner in points, albeit with question marks over that form, she may need time to settle into hurdling having failed to complete at Downpatrick last time, over six weeks ago. Jumping remains the obvious query before she can be fully trusted in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Jet To Glory
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner carrying Brian Hayes; four runs on Good with a second at 18f suggesting stamina is adequate, but finishing fourth and fifth in the two most recent starts hints she may not see out a pressured 2m4½f.
runners_data.comment: Rock-bottom of our field, though she did show a little when fourth, beaten thirteen lengths, in a bumper at Downpatrick last time. Good ground and two miles should suit, and the yard was successful in this race last year, but there's plenty for her to find here.

runners_data.name: Jo's Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tongue-tie and a solid consistent profile — two seconds and a third from six Good-ground starts; A J Martin's yard is not firing at 0/7 over 14 days but Jo's Secret's reliable finishing deserves respect.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures, this admirably consistent mare's hurdling form was later franked at a higher level, and she matched it when fourth, beaten seven and a half lengths, in a bumper at Downpatrick last time. Today's trip and ground are already covered, plus a first-time tongue-tie, and she rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Red Acres Georgie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Anthony Mullins who was absent 140 days; one Good-ground run (7th at 2m2f) offers little but the trainer knows a maiden and J J Slevin on a fresh, held-up mare over this trip merits watching.
runners_data.comment: A winner in points but well held when tried from out in front last time, a beaten seventh in a bumper at Gowran Park. Suited by two miles two on yielding, and back from a four-month absence, there's scope for more now sent hurdling, though she has plenty to find against these.

runners_data.name: Riverwoods
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe partners this De Bromhead prominent runner who has placed twice from four Good-ground starts; the form is honest if uninspiring and the trainer's three runners in 14 days shows current activity.
runners_data.comment: Ridden more positively than before, she stayed on but faded late for a third, beaten eight and a half lengths, in a bumper at Tramore last time after a break. There's more to come with that run under her belt, and with today's ground suiting, she has claims on her best hurdling form.

runners_data.name: She's All Talk Sir
runners_data.note: Unknown going profile and no recorded form; Kevin Sexton and Rory Devine hold limited data to work from, making any positional prediction speculative.
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Jukebox Jury on her first start, this mare is half-sister to Snap Fish, a fair performer at three miles. The yard is a little quiet currently, so she's perhaps one to note on this debut, with more to assess once she's had a run under these conditions.

runners_data.name: Star Of Idaho
runners_data.note: W P Mullins runner with one Good-ground start (4th at 2m), style currently unknown; Mullins has one from 16 in the 14-day window but the yard's quality differential over rivals here is a legitimate latent factor.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her sole start, beaten nine and a quarter lengths in a bumper at Wexford, this mare is with a powerful stable and expected to progress significantly now up in trip over hurdles. Conditions look right for her, though the thin experience is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Uno Me I Like My T
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade flag and a difficult recent form string (fell, fell, third, pulled up); 27 days fresh but the record offers little confidence and the amateur rider adds risk in a 19-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Struggling to make an impression under rules, having fallen in a novice chase at Punchestown last time out. There was a place in a point beforehand, but with two recent falls and hurdles chances not yet realised, she's hard to trust in this company.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's second string here, prominent in style, two runs on Good (5th and 5th); modest form but fresh enough at 20 days and the Elliott/De Bromhead axis over the Bellewstown summer track is always relevant.
runners_data.comment: Matched market expectations when comfortably held up in trip in a maiden hurdle at Downpatrick last time. There should be more to offer back up in distance again, with two to two and a quarter miles on good ground suiting, though two runs without troubling the judge is the query.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a fade flag; finished 9th on Good at 19f last time, and the combination of the younger age penalty in weight terms and the stamina query makes this a speculative proposition.
runners_data.comment: Plenty to work on after an inexperienced, error-strewn debut well beaten in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan, her only run to date. Time and further experience look the key requirements before she can be seriously considered in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Everyday Life
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced runner for Ian Donoghue with a fade flag; ninth on Good at 19f last time out suggests she is not yet competitive at this level and the trip extension to 2m4½f is uncharted.
runners_data.comment: A repeatedly placed performer in points, she brings solid form into this sphere even though her rules debut brought only a well-beaten ninth at Downpatrick three weeks ago. There should be more to come as she adapts to hurdling, but proving that under rules remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade flag and three runs on Good (11th, 12th at 2m2f and 2m6f); Dermot McLoughlin's string is modestly performing and there is little in the record to suggest she can reverse that trend today.
runners_data.comment: Little encouragement so far, with jumping errors contributing to a well-beaten effort in a maiden hurdle at Punchestown last time out. Nothing in the formline yet points to a change in fortunes, leaving her tricky to fancy among these on what she has shown to date.

runners_data.name: Prophetess Miriam
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two seconds and a second from five Good-ground runs including placed efforts over 2m; the step to 2m4½f is the key unknown and the lack of a jockey listed warrants monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Overracing troubles undid her when pulling her way forward and finishing down the field in a maiden hurdle at Punchestown last time. She showed enough in bumpers to warrant a chance on that evidence, but hasn't yet translated it over hurdles, and settling remains the key issue.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: W P Mullins hold-up mare absent 221 days; both career runs came on Good or Soft at 2m, and the extended layoff at this marathon trip in a big field demands fitness be taken on trust from the trainer's word.
runners_data.comment: Overkeen throughout and comfortably held once more in a bumper at Tramore last time, this filly is with a leading stable that may find more from her now sent hurdling. A lengthy seven-month absence adds to the queries, but a change of discipline could bring improvement over the minimum trip.

races.paceDynamic: Jet To Glory and Ardeen Joy are the two confirmed front-runners in an otherwise prominently-loaded 19-runner field, and with Jack Kennedy aboard Ardeen Joy and Brian Hayes on Jet To Glory, neither handler will concede the lead without a fight — an honest, pressured gallop from the outset is the likely product. Western Shores, Chisel Hill, Jo's Secret, Riverwoods, and Prophetess Miriam all want to be prominent, meaning the early sections will be genuinely competitive as multiple horses seek position on a track where rail berths and early pace count. The contested lead over 2m4½f on Good ground typically strings the field out, drains the front-runners in the closing stages, and sets the race up for horses who can travel smoothly in mid-division and produce a sustained run from two out rather than a sharp sprint. The race shape therefore most clearly favours hold-up and midfield horses who handle a true gallop and come with a run off the pace — closers and off-the-pace types are advantaged, provided they have the class to close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jet To Glory and Ardeen Joy force a genuine gallop that burns off the prominent runners, midfield and hold-up horses come through to dominate
scenarios.body: The two front-runners take each other on through the early and middle sections at an honest clip, leaving the prominent brigade flat in the straight as the race swings in favour of those who have been held up travelling.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace settles into a rhythm without becoming truly attritional, prominent horses who have tracked the front pair can sustain their effort to the line
scenarios.body: Chisel Hill, Riverwoods, or Jo's Secret sit just off the two leaders and, with energy in reserve entering the straight, prove too well-placed for closers to reel in over the final two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Ardeen Joy with Kennedy aboard) is allowed to dictate an uncontested or controlled gallop, they can conserve enough to hold on
scenarios.body: Ardeen Joy has five runs on Good going with two places and travels well within herself on that surface, and Kennedy is adept at judging fractions; if Jet To Glory fails to match her early, she can dictate and prove hard to reel in over the stiff final climb.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unexposed runners such as Star Of Idaho or She's All Talk Sir has untapped ability that exceeds what the formbook shows, they can exploit the pace scenario to land a surprise
scenarios.body: A field of maiden mares carries inherent uncertainty and an unexposed runner from a powerful yard (W P Mullins with Star Of Idaho) can outrun a moderate form line if the pace scenario suits their unknown style; the true gallop would allow such a horse to mark time in midfield and produce a fresh, uncomplicated run.

watchPoints.text: Ardeen Joy and Jet To Glory — watch the initial stride for which front-runner blinks first; if neither concedes, the gallop could become genuinely scorching and compromise both their finishing efforts.
Red Acres Georgie — J J Slevin on a hold-up mare fresh off a 140-day break is a classic dark-horse setup; watch her early position and whether she travels sweetly once the leaders commit.

Prophetess Miriam — no jockey listed at time of analysis; if a leading conditional or senior jockey is declared, her consistent prominent form over Good ground (four placed from five) becomes more interesting at what may be a big price.
Star Of Idaho — W P Mullins lightly raced unknown; watch if she is supported in the market, as yard placement in a maiden of this size often signals a degree of confidence even when the form is bare.

Chisel Hill — with Ardeen Joy and Jet To Glory burning petrol up front, Chisel Hill's position tracking them in second or third gear is the key positional battle to monitor; if she gets a cheap lead-stalking berth she becomes the prominent horse most likely to benefit from a pace collapse.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Riyami
runners_data.note: Top-rated in recent similar-going runs at this trip and showed course awareness, but the hold-up style and Denis Hogan yard form (T14: 2/15) means he needs a proper pace to deliver — Good ground suits per sim-going record.
runners_data.comment: A confirmed hold-up performer who races fairly off this mark, still a maiden over hurdles despite plenty of chances. His latest effort, down the field in a Flat handicap at Limerick, fell below him, but course, trip and ground are all proven, and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are added for this switch.

runners_data.name: Brohatna
runners_data.note: Michael Kenneally partners this hold-up type fresh off a 19-day turnaround; sim-going record on Good is a worry (0W0P in four) and the horse has failed to make the frame in both recent outings over this type of trip.
runners_data.comment: Matched his level again when fourth, beaten seven lengths, in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, and the opening mark looks workable on that evidence. He tends to pull hard, though, so today's longer trip is questionable, with two to two and a quarter miles on good ground his true zone.

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi
runners_data.note: Benjamin Kennedy claim adds value here; won over 20f Good ground and has a sim-going strike rate suggesting competence — the 28-day break is not a concern and Paul Flynn's yard has been active (T14: 1/13).
runners_data.comment: Full of running for a long way, this gelding was outstayed up in trip in a truly run race at Punchestown last time, caught close home and beaten three and a quarter lengths off this mark. Course, trip and ground all suit, and there's more to come once switched to fences.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Honey
runners_data.note: Simon Cavanagh double-runner alongside Clone Cross; prominent style suits the expected race shape and she has placed twice over similar trips on Good, though seven starts without a recent win may temper confidence.
runners_data.comment: Matched expectations before fading late, beaten eight lengths back from a break in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time. Decent ground and two and a half miles both suit, her mark looks fair on chasing form, and that run under her belt should bring further improvement.

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in the race — Aidan Kelly will have the run to himself from the front, but jumping errors have peppered his form and he has a history of not completing, making him a risk to back but a key tactical reference.
runners_data.comment: Rated among the leading threats on his maiden form, with a fair mark to boot, this gelding failed to complete at Sligo last time, though that race may have come too soon. He needs to turn that below-par effort around, but with course, trip and ground all suited, he rates highly on official figures.

runners_data.name: Hitthehayson
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with two wins and five places on Good ground over 20-22f; Josh Williamson partners a horse who has been in the frame in his last two comparable runs and is ideally drawn for this scenario.
runners_data.comment: Back on song when dropped in trip for a good second at Downpatrick last time, beaten four and a quarter lengths, this gelding is our top-rated runner and in good form this season. Course, trip and ground are all proven, and he rates tough to peg back, with first-time cheekpieces the only slight unknown.

runners_data.name: Soldier Saint
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finishes and hold-up style on Good — Jordan Canavan (4) takes the ride but the profile of dropping late suggests this horse will struggle to feature in the closing stages of a controlled race.
runners_data.comment: Fancied to play a role but only matched his level in a well-beaten effort in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time. Inconsistency has marked his short career so far, though today's trip and going both suit, and a first-time hood offers a fresh angle.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Jack Gilligan (2) on a horse who won last time over 18f Good and has a 1W4P sim-going record in 12-14 runs — the prominent-to-midfield position suits a scenario where pace develops and this lightly-weighted five-year-old gets a clear run.
runners_data.comment: A hefty ten-length win back down in trip and off a lower mark at Downpatrick last time makes her one to respect, with a more forceful ride bringing out her best. That was a marked turnaround from a mixed run of finishes beforehand, and repeating it remains the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Unknown style horse with three non-completions in five recent starts and a T14 strike rate of 3/27 for Andrew Slattery — no sim-going wins and likely needs more cut than Good offers to produce best form.
runners_data.comment: Overkeen and clearly needing that run back from a break, this mare was well beaten in a handicap hurdle at Limerick last time. She should strip fitter for the experience, though inconsistency has been an issue in her career and the stable is out of sorts currently, both factors against her.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from a long 436-day absence; showed ability to place on Good in the past and carries headgear (p) — the layoff is the dominant question and Patrick Rooney's yard (T14: 0/0) gives no confidence for a quick return.
runners_data.comment: Showed her best form in a while when a close second at Kilbeggan last time, beaten three and a half lengths up in trip off a higher mark, though that's well over a year ago now. First-time cheekpieces and suitable ground and trip are in her favour, but the long layoff is the query.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Long 151-day break for this fade-prone runner; Ross Berry (4) takes the ride but sim-going record (0W0P) and the tendency to weaken late make this a difficult proposition in a Good-ground race at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete in a maiden hurdle at Fairyhouse last time, her jumping letting her down that day, and she's yet to show anything of real note across a mixed set of finishes. A first switch to handicaps could bring about an improvement, but proving it remains the challenge after five months on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: Ballinagaine Girl
runners_data.note: John Hanlon's charge placed last time on Soft and is clearly capable, but her natural rear-of-field style means she is being run out of position in a field saturated with hold-up horses — the style displacement (STYLE_FIT 0.92) is real and tempers her winning chance here regardless of form.
runners_data.comment: A close second, beaten a neck off a lower mark, at Limerick last time marked a step up from her previous efforts, and she'd be a major player building further on it. Course, distance and two and a half miles are all in her favour, though repeating that level is the query.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old with back-to-back thirds on Good ground at 18-20f; Patrick O'Brien (2) takes the ride and Adrian McGuinness has been in good form (T14: 2/28) — the hold-up profile is a concern in a steady-pace race but the form trajectory is upward.
runners_data.comment: Matched his level again with a third, beaten four and a quarter lengths, in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time, having shown similarly the run before. He'd be dangerous building further on that pair of efforts, with course, trip and ground all suited, though the stable's current lean spell is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Triple non-completer in five recent starts and fade-prone with blinkers; Shane O'Callaghan partners a horse who has a 0W0P sim-going record and gives little reason to believe the pattern will change over this trip today.
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete yet again last time in a handicap hurdle at Tramore, extending a wretched run of finishes in this grade. Blinkers are added for the first time in a bid to spark an improvement, and two to two and a half miles suits, but there's little in the formline to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who finishes races — Eoghan Finegan (2) rides and the nine-run sim-going record (0W1P) shows durability if not brilliance; the 38-day break is manageable and the horse needs the pace to genuinely develop to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Setting the pace and used up too soon, she was comfortably held in a handicap hurdle at Wexford last time. With a capable stable behind her, and course, trip and decent ground all suited, there's scope for a turnaround, but her recent run of finishes offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Carries top weight (OR=100) but Carl Millar (2) partners a prominent type who placed last time over 16f Good — the 50-day break is slightly concerning but Cian Collins has shown ability with horses off breaks (T14: 0/4) and the prominent style suits the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Stepped down in grade and trip when a close second, beaten just half a length, in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan last time - a much better effort than his earlier starts suggested. A mixed record and top weight on a testing opening mark are the concerns, even with first-time cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Agent Tequila
runners_data.note: Dylan Kidd (4) rides a fade-prone hold-up horse returning from 109 days off — the true rear-of-field tendency is the dominant issue here as the horse is effectively racing displaced in the midfield pack, and the long absence adds further risk.
runners_data.comment: Successful in a point-to-point but yet to show much of that form under rules, failing to complete last time in a handicap chase at Wexford, needing that run after a break. He's normally held up, and today's course, trip and ground are proven, with first-time cheekpieces the fresh angle, but he still has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: John Hanlon's second string alongside Ballinagaine Girl; the prominent headgear (p) signals a horse managed up front in theory but the natural hold-up profile forces displacement into midfield — sim-going record over 22f Good is extensive (14/15 runs) with three places but no wins.
runners_data.comment: A series of jumping errors undid her last time, failing to find much in a handicap chase at Tramore and finishing well beaten. She remains a maiden despite plenty of starts, though today's course, trip and ground are all proven and first-time cheekpieces are added in search of sharper jumping.

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: Fade-prone hold-up horse with a 0W0P sim-going record in four qualifying runs; the redistribution into midfield masks a true rear-of-field tendency and connections have no recent runners (T14: 0/0), making this among the least likely winners in the field.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten yet again in a handicap hurdle at Limerick last time, continuing a run of finishes that has shown little to note. Everything remains to be proven on this evidence, leaving her hard to fancy in this line-up.

races.paceDynamic: Clone Cross is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and faces no direct head-to-head pace pressure, meaning Simon Cavanagh's runner can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front over the 2m4½f trip on Good turf at Bellewstown. Hitthehayson and Codger's Rock are genuine prominent types likely to track closely behind, while Hurricane Honey and My Policy will also seek early positions, creating an organised but not chaotic pace scenario. The field contains significantly more hold-up and prominent types than the race map can accommodate — Ballinagaine Girl, Mother Ship, Agent Tequila, and Lost Features are natural rear-of-field horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in practice they will need to race further back than their shown positions, making them reliant on a strong pace developing late. With one unhurried pace-setter and a steady gallop likely, this race shape favours prominent racers who can track the leader within striking distance and pounce from the second or third flight of hurdles out — hold-up horses dependent on a true test are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clone Cross Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Clone Cross leads at a steady clip and the prominent brigade track efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: Clone Cross sets an uncontested rhythm and the race becomes a procession for those travelling just behind — Hitthehayson and Codger's Rock are ideally placed to kick from two out without burning excessive energy in transit. This scenario rewards horses with tactical speed and good jumping who can exploit a race run at a manageable clip, rather than those needing deep stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stayers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Clone Cross is taken on or the early gallop is faster than anticipated, stretching the field and producing a stamina test from three out.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would expose Clone Cross's inconsistent jumping record and bring the stayers into play as the field strings out approaching the final turn. Pourquoi Poi and Granlahan, who have shown ability to stay and finish on Good ground, would benefit from the extra emphasis on endurance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Produce Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and a gap opens in the straight for horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A true gallop would increase oxygen debt in the prominent racers and allow a well-positioned midfield horse to mow them down in the closing stages over this testing 2m4½f trip. Whiskey Serenade and Georginas Jet have each shown ability to finish on Good ground and would be the most credible beneficiaries, carrying more realistic map positions than the redistributed hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistributed Hold-Ups Land
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches on a tight early pace and the genuine rear-runners somehow find clear racing room through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: This low-probability shape requires both a collapsing pace and clean passage for horses racing out of their natural role — Ballinagaine Girl and Mother Ship are capable on form but are structurally disadvantaged by the crowded midfield they are forced to occupy. The style-fit discount on these runners makes this scenario the least likely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Clone Cross — monitor at every flight; if he makes a jumping error in the early stages or gets headed before two out, the controlled race shape collapses entirely and the prominent trackers will face a different test than anticipated.

Hitthehayson — carrying headgear (p) and has been placed in seven of fifteen Good-ground runs; if he travels smoothly just off Clone Cross from the third flight, he is the horse most likely to dictate the result from the front two positions.

Codger's Rock — top weight and 50-day break is a watch combination; if he moves fluently early under Carl Millar and positions behind Clone Cross without being pushed, his 2m4½f form profile makes him a live each-way danger.

Granlahan — four-year-old with improving form in last two runs and a connected trainer firing (T14: 2/28); if the pace quickens in the back straight and he switches off in the midfield, watch for a forward move from three out.

Ballinagaine Girl and Mother Ship — both Hanlon runners and both genuine hold-up types running from a compromised position; if either travels much closer to the pace than expected, the jockey has made a tactical adjustment worth noting early on.

races.name: QuinnBet Bellewstown Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lisnagar Fortune
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race; John McConnell yard 2/25 in 14 days and horse ran 26 days ago — freshness counts; Good-ground form is solid (3/20f/GOO in sim-going) and the style fit of 0.93 reflects it is racing close to its natural role here, making it the key pace anchor.|
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent in four runs without a win, he was well beaten at Roscommon last time, perhaps needing that outing for fitness. First-time cheekpieces and past form over today's trip and going offer some hope, but a stable short of winners and a rating of 116 leave him with work to do.

runners_data.name: Outside The Door
runners_data.note: 10-year-old with strong Good-ground record (13/15 sim-going, 3W7P) and won over 26f on Good last time out 65 days ago; prominent style sits naturally behind the leader and the P Smithers claim of 7lb is a meaningful weight-pull at OR 116.|
runners_data.comment: Back on the faster ground he prefers, he confirmed his well-being when second in a cross-country chase at Punchestown latest. Now dropped to hurdles off a mark that looks lenient, with first-time blinkers and course-and-distance form on his side, he heads this at 125 after only a brief break.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability
runners_data.note: 5-year-old improver who won on Good over 20f last time, 35 days ago; races prominently and has placed twice on Good ground in five runs — the youth and form trajectory are positives, but stepping up to 3m½f is uncharted territory.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame this term, he won a maiden hurdle at Listowel by two lengths last time on ground he handles well, helped by a fallen rival. Handicapping now off a mark that looks lenient, he's a genuine threat at 123, with that facile scoreline the main question.

runners_data.name: Ottoman Style
runners_data.note: A decade-old handicapper whose Good-ground record reads 8/15 (0W2P) — moderate; pulled up or unfinished runs pepper the recent history and the tongue-tie plus hood suggest a horse needing everything to go right over this marathon trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts, he was eased when pulled up at Punchestown last time, with something clearly amiss. He's suited by cut but also handles decent ground, and first-time blinkers plus a tongue-tie could sharpen him, though there's plenty to prove off a rating of 116.

runners_data.name: Jisco Du Brem
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on Good 39 days ago and holds two wins in five Good-ground outings; races prominently and is suited by this trip and conditions — tongue-tie worn consistently, trainer 0/0 in 14-day window but horse arrives in good order.|
runners_data.comment: Stepping up in trip and down in grade paid off when he landed a handicap by three lengths off a lower mark at Ballinrobe last time, and today's longer distance should suit him even better. On a fair mark and unfazed by cut in the ground, he's a leading threat at 118, with harder company the obvious test.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground in sim-going history (3/5) but has been off 278 days (27 starts flag likely an error — treat as a long absence); visor worn and OR 110 is manageable, but fitness after such a break is a genuine question mark at 3m½f.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last five starts put him in good order, though he was beaten eight lengths in a handicap at Navan last time on his first spin on the level since last spring. A yard in form and first-time visor offer some hope, but a rating of 110 leaves plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Le Kap
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner with Darragh O'Keeffe aboard — strong booking at OR 109; all four runs on Good have produced 0W0P but the horse is only 6 and showed a third on soft over 20f; prominent style suits the projected race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in four starts, he was comfortably held in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel last time, with that run possibly bringing him forward off a break. He handles today's ground and a rating of 111 keeps him competitive, with the form of his earlier efforts said to be working out well.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse, the clearest natural beneficiary of the controlled-pace scenario; Brian Barry's 7lb claim helps at OR 108, and Good-ground form over 24f (1W4P in 13 runs) shows it acts on the surface — pulled up twice recently needs explaining but recent 5th and 6th suggest it retains ability.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he ran to a fair level when beaten nine lengths in a handicap hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, having had a lot of ground to make up. A good mark on his form over fences, first-time cheekpieces and tongue-tie, plus course-and-distance experience over this longer trip, work in his favour, and he's respected at 113.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: Naturally a front-runner — pushed into midfield on the map purely because the prominent slots are full; OR 108 5-year-old whose recent form is over shorter trips (12-13f) on Good, so stamping 3m½f is a significant unknown, and the out-of-role positioning blunts its chance.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed record over hurdles, including a win three runs back, was undermined when she parted with her jockey at Downpatrick last time, leaving her form hard to trust. She races well on good ground at shorter trips, and a rating of 111 keeps her in the mix, but the inconsistency is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Whatsavailable
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Good-ground staying form (3W over 24f in sim-going); OR 106 for M F Morris, unraced for 35 days — the style is genuine and the trip suits, making this one of the cleaner profile fits for a prominent/late scenario.|
