runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, he raced too freely and was caught late when fourth, beaten 28 lengths, in a handicap hurdle at Listowel latest. He's up to today's trip and ground, and first-time cheekpieces plus tongue-tie could help settle him, with a workable rating of 110 offering a sliver of hope if his level does hold up.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer whose natural front-of-field role has been displaced — forced into midfield by the sheer volume of similar types; Good-ground record reads 12/14 (1W6P) but the 9th and 10th finishes in the last two suggest a loss of form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he jumped and travelled poorly, finishing down the field in a handicap chase at Tramore last time, on a track that may not have suited. Earlier form was better, and he handles decent ground up to today's trip, but a rating of 102 - bottom of this field - leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: The Miracle Man
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott (3/29 in 14 days) — strong handler/jockey combination; this is a natural front-runner bumped to midfield by the crowded prominent group, but if Kennedy can creep forward early the Good-ground form (2W3P in 7 runs) is competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent without a win in five runs, he was well beaten down the field in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time, a below-par effort after solid form before that. First-time blinkers, a notable jockey booking and course-and-distance form on ground he handles all boost his claims, with a rating of 111 keeping him in the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a top booking but the horse arrives 109 days fresh having finished unplaced in five of its last six; pushed out of its natural prominent role into midfield, and the combination of layoff and out-of-role mapping makes this a difficult profile to trust.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in easier company but yet to fire now handicapping, he was well beaten down the field in a handicap hurdle at Down Royal last time, his first try at this level. A long break since, a stayer's profile and conditions he handles offer hope, and a rating of 111 keeps him in the mix if that maiden form transfers.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: 6-year-old with three Good-ground runs (0W1P) — very limited evidence; naturally a prominent racer held in midfield by field congestion, and the David O'Brien yard has had one winner from five in 14 days, but the sample size on this horse is too small to project confidently.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he stepped forward again when upped in trip, finishing second beaten two lengths in a maiden hurdle at Tramore last time. Now sent handicapping for the first time with even further ground to travel in his favour, he could progress again, though a modest rating of 102 keeps him towards the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Accustomed
runners_data.note: 5/24f on Good last time and ran 2nd over 20f in similar conditions — the stamina evidence is there; however this is another natural prominent type crowded out of position, and the 0W2P Good-ground record alongside a 27-day turnaround leaves the profile in the mid-tier.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below his maiden form, he was ridden for the longer haul when beaten just over nine lengths in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown last time, having had too much ground to make up. Course-and-distance form, conditions he handles and first-time cheekpieces make him a big threat at 117 for all his modest mark, with a lack of a win his one query.

runners_data.name: Justatan
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins runner back after 160 days — a significant layoff; all five sim-going runs came on Heavy or soft (1/5 on Good), so the ground switch is a real concern, and the hold-up style means it needs everything to pan out perfectly after a long absence.|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, his first handicap proved tough, finishing down the field in a handicap hurdle at Naas last time. A long absence and a step up in trip make this a fresh test, and though a shrewd yard could find improvement, his best form has come at shorter trips, leaving him hard to fancy at 107.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: McConnell's second string (same trainer as Lisnagar Fortune, yard 2/25 in 14 days); 10-year-old whose Good-ground record is 11/15 (1W1P) — limited upside; a natural front-runner consigned to midfield by the field's pace density, and consistent place-without-winning form suggests a frustrating type.|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, he lacked the gears for a shorter trip and was well held in a handicap hurdle at Wexford last time, a drop in distance that clearly didn't suit. He wants at least today's longer trip, and with course-and-distance form, first-time cheekpieces and a mark with room to rise, he has claims at 111, that below-par run perhaps bringing him forward.

races.paceDynamic: Lisnagar Fortune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, should dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over the 3m½f trip on Good ground at Bellewstown. The pace map holds a significant volume of prominent-style horses — Radar Ahead, The Miracle Man, Midnight Moonshine, Mavetherave, Tolka Row, Accustomed and Broken Ice are all natural up-with-the-pace types who cannot all occupy their preferred early positions, meaning several will be shuffled back and forced to race against their instincts. Outside The Door, Burning Ability, Ottoman Style, Jisco Du Brem, Mephisto and Le Kap provide a secondary prominent group that will filter into the positions just behind Lisnagar Fortune, creating a moderately strung-out race with a predictable front-end structure rather than a contested early gallop. This shape — a lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo with hold-up and back-of-midfield horses unable to get competitive cover early — strongly favours genuine hold-up horses who settle, travel fluidly through traffic and possess a clean staying kick in the final half-mile; Dorans Law, Whatsavailable and Justatan are the clearest beneficiaries of this dynamic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stayers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Lisnagar Fortune leads unopposed at a steady clip and the race only quickens in the final mile, allowing genuine stayers racing from hold-up or deep midfield to reel in the front group.
scenarios.body: Lisnagar Fortune sets a frugal pace that keeps the prominent pack bunched and conservative, and those with stamina to sustain a run from off the pace — unbothered by early traffic — arrive with the most horse turning for home; Dorans Law and Whatsavailable are the archetype beneficiaries of this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lisnagar Fortune gets away cleanly, finds a comfortable rhythm and the pursuers fail to mount a coordinated challenge due to the traffic caused by the over-crowded prominent group.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of so many front-runners into midfield creates a chaotic pursuit pack that blocks and checks each other, allowing the uncontested leader to find enough to hold on; Lisnagar Fortune's 26-day freshness and good-ground form (3/20f/GOO) support this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Escapee Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the natural prominent types who was redistributed to midfield manages to creep forward early and secure a position close to the pace before the field settles.
scenarios.body: A horse like The Miracle Man or Jisco Du Brem — comfortable racing prominently on Good ground over staying trips — positions itself within striking distance of Lisnagar Fortune and uses superior class or recency to hit the front at the last flight; this scenario is partially constrained by the number of horses competing for the same ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Front
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves deceptively strong or Lisnagar Fortune is pressured into an unsustainable gallop that fractures the field in the final mile.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace would string out the field quickly, leaving those who settled furthest back with the most ground to make up but fresh legs to do so; Justatan, despite limited good-ground evidence, and Whatsavailable could benefit, though a true pace collapse is the least likely shape given the single front-runner dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Dorans Law and Whatsavailable are the two genuine hold-up horses in a race dominated by prominent types — watch whether Brian Barry and Josh Williamson can find clear passage in the straight, because a traffic-free run could see them arrive with a decisive advantage.|

Lisnagar Fortune must be tracked from the gate — if it jumps sluggishly or loses the lead to a bold-jumping rival such as Outside The Door or Burning Ability, the entire pace map shifts and the race becomes more competitive early than projected.|

The Miracle Man with Jack Kennedy is the most dangerous of the redistributed prominent horses — watch whether Kennedy ignores the map and sends him forward from the outset; if he secures a position just behind Lisnagar Fortune, the Elliott/Kennedy combination becomes a live threat.|

Mephisto's fitness is a serious unknown after 278 days absent — watch the market moves and paddock demeanour closely, as a non-runner or visibly underdone horse would remove one of the OR 110 prominent competitors and slightly ease the pace congestion.|

Justatan's 160-day layoff combined with poor Good-ground evidence (1/5) means Emmet Mullins must be trusted on a run-to-fitness basis — monitor whether it settles kindly for Ricky Doyle or pulls early, as an ungainly hold-up horse at 3m½f after a long break could become a jumping hazard in the pack.|

runners_data.name: Caman Hill
runners_data.comment: A debut win that has since been franked by subsequent form marks him as a smart prospect, and he confirmed that promise when fourth, beaten 11 lengths, in a step up in grade under penalty in a bumper at Listowel last time. Course-and-distance form on ground he handles and clear room for improvement make him a big threat at 119.

runners_data.name: Dee Bee Zed
runners_data.comment: An eye-catching surprise on his only start, he won a bumper at Punchestown by three lengths on debut, a shock result that may still undersell his true ability. Course-and-distance form and ground he handles are in his favour, leaving him fairly assessed at 113 with more expected to come.

runners_data.name: Rokanako
runners_data.comment: Building on a debut experience, he took advantage of a pace meltdown to land a bumper at Kilbeggan by three lengths last time, though that form looks modest on inspection. He does have course-and-distance claims and acts well on this ground, but a rating of just 110 leaves him hard to fancy against this field.

runners_data.name: Fortysixnchange
runners_data.comment: A promising debut win in a bumper at Wexford by three lengths leaves room for more, even if that form carries a few question marks. His yard has landed this race before, and back after a break, he's a fair contender at 113.

runners_data.name: Begorrah Boy
runners_data.comment: A first-time runner out of a dam who failed to complete in points, he's by Conduit for a yard better known for point success but capable of readying sorts for a bumper debut. There's some interest in him at 111, though he remains up in the air on account of his complete lack of experience.

runners_data.name: Go Loud
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five runs, he shaped better than the result suggests when beaten seven lengths in a bumper at Punchestown last time, having shown a little promise in points before that. Course-and-distance conditions suit, and there should be more to come, leaving him with claims at 112.

runners_data.name: I Give Theorders
runners_data.comment: Rated on potential rather than the form shown, he was green and never involved in a bumper at Clonmel most recent, though that inexperience is easily forgiven. There's plenty for connections to unlock yet, and after a break to sharpen him, he's a leading contender at 115 - his modest form to date the obvious catch.

runners_data.name: Sir Vinny
runners_data.comment: An eye-catching third on his sole start, beaten just three and a half lengths in a bumper at Punchestown, points to a bright future. Conditions and course-and-distance form suit, and there should be more to come with that debut experience now banked, making him a leading threat at 118.

runners_data.name: Woodie Wiley
runners_data.comment: Little to work with so far, he was travelling in midfield at a big price when he lost his footing mid-race on his bumper debut, and drew a blank in his point starts beforehand. There's not much evidence to build a case on, leaving him one to monitor rather than fully trust at 115.

runners_data.name: Yanure
runners_data.comment: Winless in two starts, he couldn't build on a strong debut when down the field in a bumper at Thurles last time, and returns now after a lengthy break. That solid opening effort suggests a bounce-back is possible, and course-and-distance conditions are in his corner, but a rating of just 110 makes him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Hot Rock Harry
runners_data.comment: Overly keen and well beaten on his only start, in a bumper for four-year-olds at Down Royal, he clearly has more to offer for a powerful stable. His connections have a solid record in this event, and course-and-distance conditions suit, but a modest rating of 105 leaves him with a mountain to climb.

runners_data.name: Mr Enigma
runners_data.comment: A half-brother to Fourtowns, who was fair over two miles, he's out of a dam placed in a bumper and bred by Pillar Coral. With no racing form yet to judge, he's one to note on debut rather than fully trusted at 115.

runners_data.name: Mila Ballerina
runners_data.comment: Raw and well beaten on her only start, in a bumper at Punchestown, she clearly needed that experience under her belt. First-time visor and a fresh opportunity give her a chance to progress, but she still has plenty to prove at 115 after that below-par debut.

runners_data.name: Pamelaisbrass
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her sole start, in a bumper at Naas, she has a stack of ground to find on that evidence. A lengthy break since could bring improvement, but with major progress still needed, she's up against it at 115 on what she has shown so far.

runners_data.name: Silk Buds
runners_data.comment: A creditable third, beaten eight and a quarter lengths, in a maiden bumper at Kelso last time hinted at more to come after a flawed debut. Course-and-distance conditions suit and she's fresh from a break, but a modest rating of 107 leaves her with work to do against this field.

runners_data.name: Kingside Lady
runners_data.comment: Boosted form from a six-length win in a maiden at Ballindenisk gives her a standout profile, and she joins a yard capable of producing first-time-out bumper winners, with a strong record in this race too. On all known evidence she's the one to beat at 128, with the step up into this company the only thing left to confirm.
